changes.old: The short readout interval is not a short lifetime of the underlying integrator. A tuned integrator can continue to represent the mean of accumulated inputs while its variance grows. A leak would instead pull its mean toward a particular value. Diffusion limits the accuracy of the integral and the usefulness of long observation; it does not by itself introduce that restoring pull. Applying these predictions to an animal also requires checking its spike statistics, tuning, drift, access to spikes, and other sources of movement noise.[^p1-integrator]
changes.new: When a continuous attractor circuit is used to accumulate an incoming signal over time, its stored value represents the integral of that signal. The short useful readout interval does not imply a short lifetime for this accumulated value. A tuned circuit can continue to represent the mean of accumulated inputs while its variance grows. A leak would instead pull its mean toward a particular value. Diffusion limits the accuracy of the integral and the usefulness of long observation; it does not by itself introduce that restoring pull. Applying these predictions to an animal also requires checking its spike statistics, tuning, drift, access to spikes, and other sources of movement noise.[^p1-integrator]
changes.reason: Explain the input and stored result in plain language; retain all mean, variance, leak and empirical limits without adding a formal term. The glossary oculomotor-integrator entry was checked and not changed.
